newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch propose 1,000 ha expansion to Rotterdam port.
newsitem.headline: Dutch propose 1,000 ha expansion to Rotterdam port.

text.p: The Dutch cabinet council has recommended that Rotterdam port be allowed to expand by 1,000 hectares, the Dutch ministry of transport said on Friday.

The decision, which would entail reclamation of land from the sea, comes in response to calls from the Rotterdam port authority and the city of Rotterdam that the city's harbour activities are running out of space.
"The cabinet considers it (expansion) of great importance for a sustainable and responsible strengthening of the Dutch economy," the Dutch ministry of transport said in a statement.
The port authority plans to use the new land for container and chemicals traffic.
The cabinet council has also proposed reclaiming a further 750 hectares of land for nature and recreational use.
The government should reach a final decision in 1999, subject to parliamentary approval, which could see the emergence of the first stretch of the land, referred to as the Maasvlakte Twee, by 2002.
The full 1,750 hectare reclamation is expected to cost between four and five billion guilders ($2-2.5 billion) of which Rotterdam says it would to pay a quarter.
The government has so far not said to what extent it would finance the project.
"That depends on the level of public interest," said a transport ministry spokesman.

The expansion steers a course between the demands of the Rotterdam port authority -- which had urged that an extra 2,000 hectares of industrial and harbour area be built -- and environmentalists, who believed no expansion should take place.
The city of Rotterdam said on Friday it was happy with the preliminary decision.
"The cabinet has recognised that Rotterdam harbour is of national importance," a spokesman said.
